transcript.title: Operator
transcript.content: Good morning, and thank you for standing by. Welcome to Abbott's Second Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. During the question-and-answer session, you will be able to ask your question by pressing the star 1 keys on your touch-tone phone. This call is being recorded by Abbott. With the exception of any participants' questions asked during the question-and-answer session, the entire call, including the question-and-answer session, is material copyrighted by Abbott. It cannot be recorded or rebroadcast without Abbott's expressed written permission. I would now like to introduce Mr. Michael Comilla, Vice President, Investor Relations.

transcript.speaker: Michael Comilla
transcript.title: Vice President, Investor Relations
transcript.content: Good morning, and thank you for joining us. With me today are Robert Ford, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and Philip Boudreau, Executive Vice President, Finance, and Chief Financial Officer. Robert and Philip will provide opening remarks. Following their comments, we will take your questions. Before we get started, some statements made today may be forward-looking for purposes of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 2000, including the expected financial results for 2026. Abbott cautions that these forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially from those indicated in the forward-looking statements. Economic, competitive, governmental, technological, and other factors that may affect Abbott's operations are discussed in Item 1A, Risk Factors, in our annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 12/31/2025. Abbott undertakes no obligation to release publicly any revisions to forward-looking statements as a result of subsequent events or developments except as required by law. On today's conference call, as in the past, non-GAAP financial measures will be used to help investors understand Abbott's ongoing business performance. These non-GAAP financial measures are reconciled with comparable GAAP financial measures in our earnings news release and regulatory filings from today, which are available on our website at abbott.com. Note that Abbott has not provided the related GAAP financial measures on a forward-looking basis for the non-GAAP financial measures for which it is providing guidance because the company is unable to predict with reasonable certainty and without unreasonable effort the timing and impact of certain items, which could significantly impact Abbott's results in accordance with GAAP. Unless otherwise noted, our commentary on sales growth refers to comparable sales growth. Our definition of comparable sales growth can be found on Page 2 of our press release issued earlier today. A reconciliation table containing the data needed to calculate comparable sales growth can be found on pages 16 and 17. With that, I will now turn the call over to Robert Ford.

transcript.speaker: Robert Ford
transcript.title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
transcript.content: Okay. Mike, good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we issued second quarter results that included comparable sales growth of 4.8%, which represents an acceleration compared to the previous two quarters, and adjusted earnings per share of $1.31, which exceeded the midpoint of our guidance range and the consensus estimate. Considering our second-quarter results and updated outlook for the remainder of the year, we are reaffirming our full-year guidance for comparable sales growth of 6.5% to 7.5% and raising our EPS guidance range to $5.45 to $5.60. Before summarizing our second-quarter results, I want to highlight a few recent pipeline achievements, including completing patient enrollment in our Tectonic coronary IVL pivotal trial, completing our FDA submission for approval of our new Amulet 360 left atrial appendage device, obtaining CE Mark for Libre Duo, the world's first dual glucose-ketone monitoring sensor designed to detect rising ketone levels and help prevent diabetic ketoacidosis. We anticipate launching these three new products, along with our Tactiflex Duo PFA catheter, in the U.S. at a steady cadence over the next 12 months. We also remain on track to begin patient enrollment in the fourth quarter for several important clinical trials that will support a steady cadence of future product launches. These include a balloon-expandable TAVR valve, a leadless conduction system pacing device leveraging our Avera pacemaker, a mitral replacement valve developed following the acquisition of Cephea Valve Technologies, a peripheral IVL device developed following the acquisition of CSI, and a wearable continuous lactate monitoring sensor designed to reduce the risk of sepsis following discharge from the hospital. I will now review our second-quarter results in more detail before I turn the call over to Philip, and I will start with diagnostics. Diagnostic test results inform approximately 70% of all health care decisions, making testing volumes a reliable barometer of overall health care activity and demand. Our test volume data, which is sourced directly from our diagnostic instruments located across the United States and around the world, continues to reflect strong and stable demand for testing. We view this as a positive indication of the durable underlying demand for health care, not just in the U.S., but globally. This durable demand was evident in our core laboratory results this quarter where our U.S. business grew 7.5%, and we continue our track record of strong performance across Latin America. In rapid and molecular diagnostics, sales declined 8%, driven by the anticipated decrease in respiratory testing as a result of a weaker-than-normal season that concluded during the second quarter. In cancer diagnostics, sales growth of 13% was driven by mid-teens growth of Cologuard, which is benefiting from a growing base of both new and repeat Cologuard users as well as contributions to growth from our precision oncology and international business. We continue to expect cancer diagnostics growth in the second half of the year to be higher than the first half, supported by increasing volumes from care-gap programs, recently launched tests, and continued international adoption. In May, the American Cancer Society updated its colorectal cancer screening guidelines, reaffirming Cologuard and Cologuard Plus as preferred screening options. This designation reflects Cologuard's market-leading accuracy and superior ability to detect cancer at earlier stages compared to other available tests. Moving to nutrition, where sales finished slightly ahead of our expectations for the second consecutive quarter. Sales increased sequentially by $125 million, driven by improving performance in both pediatric and adult nutrition. In pediatric nutrition, our international business was the first of our nutrition businesses to transition back to delivering positive growth, delivering growth of 6.5% in the quarter. In U.S. pediatric, we exited the quarter with the full benefit of recent WIC contract wins reflected in our run rate, and as a result, Abbott is now the market leader in both WIC and non-WIC segments. In adult nutrition, we continue to see positive volume trends in response to the price actions implemented late last year. In the U.S., retail consumption of Ensure increased double digits compared to consumption levels exiting last year and achieved the highest year-over-year consumption growth in the past year and a half. We are also making good progress in our international adult nutrition business where sales continue to grow sequentially and are now approaching levels similar to this time last year. We are also benefiting from sales contributions from new innovation, including new versions of Ensure that feature higher protein, lower sugar, and refreshed labeling and packaging. Overall, I remain encouraged by the progress we are making and confident in our outlook for the second half of the year. Turning to EPD, where we continue to deliver consistently strong performance. Sales grew 9% in the quarter, reflecting broad-based growth across our largest markets, including India, Latin America, and Southeast Asia. This performance reflects disciplined execution by our teams and the growing demand for health care in emerging markets. This demand is a result of evolving market dynamics, including expanding access to health care, aging populations, and a rising need to treat both acute and chronic conditions. These structural tailwinds, combined with our broad portfolio, expanding pipeline of biosimilars, and strong brand equity, position EPD to sustainably deliver high single-digit sales growth. I will wrap up with medical devices where sales grew 8.5%. Growth in our cardiovascular device portfolio was led by growth in electrophysiology and high single-digit growth in rhythm management and heart failure. In electrophysiology, the second quarter marked the beginning of an acceleration in our growth trajectory. We launched our next-generation Bolt PFA catheter, commonly referred to as Bolt 2.0, in the U.S. in May, and we expect to transition from a limited market release to a full market release in the third quarter. Internationally, the expanding rollout of Bolt and Tactiflex Duo is gaining strong traction, driving growth of more than 20% in Europe. We remain confident in our outlook for the second half of the year, including our expectations to begin outperforming the market and recapturing share. In Rhythm Management, sales grew 9.5% as we continue to expand the use of Avera across both the single- and dual-chamber segments of the pacemaker market and to drive broader adoption of this innovative technology. In heart failure, growth of 9% was led by double-digit growth in the U.S., driven by our market-leading portfolio of heart-assist devices that address both chronic and acute patient needs. In diabetes care, continuous glucose monitoring sales exceeded $2 billion, reflecting growth of 9.5% in the quarter. In May, we secured CE Mark for Libre Duo, the world's first dual glucose-ketone wearable sensor. We will begin the international rollout of Libre Duo in the fall and we look forward to bringing this innovative new technology to the United States market after we obtain FDA approval. In summary, we remain highly focused on disciplined execution in each quarter. Our second-quarter results represent an important building block as we move into the second half of the year. We have momentum building across the portfolio and have a clear line of sight to the key drivers of sales growth acceleration that are forecasted in the second half. Our continued focus on gross margin expansion gives us confidence in raising our full-year EPS guidance. We have several new products that we anticipate launching at a steady cadence over the next 12 months. I will turn the call over to Philip.

transcript.speaker: Philip Boudreau
transcript.title: Executive Vice President, Finance and Chief Financial Officer
transcript.content: Thanks, Robert. As Mike mentioned earlier, please note that all references to sales growth rates, unless otherwise noted, are on a comparable basis. Turning to our second-quarter results, sales increased 4.8% on a comparable basis and adjusted earnings per share of $1.31 exceeded the midpoint of our guidance range and the consensus estimate. Foreign exchange had a favorable year-over-year impact of 0.8% on second-quarter sales, which was a slight improvement to our expectations at the time of our earnings call in April. Regarding other aspects of the P&L, the adjusted gross margin profile was 58.0% of sales, representing an increase of 100 basis points compared to the prior year. The improvement was broad-based, reflecting favorable business mix within the legacy Abbott portfolio and from the addition of Exact Sciences, as well as the continued operational improvements and discipline of our margin expansion initiatives. Adjusted R&D was 6.9% of sales, and adjusted SG&A was 28.6% of sales. Based on current rates, we expect exchange to have a positive impact of 1% on full-year sales, which includes our expectation for exchange to have a negative impact of approximately 1% on third-quarter sales. For the third quarter, we forecast adjusted earnings per share of $1.38 to $1.46. With that, we will now open the call for questions.

transcript.speaker: Operator
transcript.title: Operator
transcript.content: Thank you. At this time, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, press star 1. You will then hear an automated message advising you that your hand is raised. To withdraw your question, please press star 1 again. For optimal sound quality, we kindly ask that you use your handset instead of your speakerphone when asking your question. Our first question comes from Robert Marcus from JPMorgan. Your line is open.

transcript.speaker: Robert Marcus
transcript.title: Analyst (JPMorgan)
transcript.content: Great. Good morning. Thank you very much for taking the questions. Robert, if I may, two questions: one market question, one Abbott question. If I start with the market question, I think a theme that a lot of investors are focused on given some of the negative preannouncements out of the hospital sector is the potential for decelerating procedure volumes, particularly in the U.S. We heard from J&J yesterday that they are not seeing any sign of that. We heard from you this morning, particularly on the diagnostic volumes where you have a great view into forward-looking volumes, it sounds like you are not seeing anything. I would love to hear your view on the health and the forecast of procedure volumes in the U.S. and what you are seeing and expecting. Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Robert Ford
transcript.title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
transcript.content: Sure. That seems to be a topic of concern for investors, but it is less of a concern for the companies operating in the markets where we are active. I think there are a couple reasons for that. Some concern about a decline in volumes is tied to challenges with ACA enrollment or disenrollment in Medicaid. I think that is a flawed assumption as it relates to the med tech and diagnostic space. When the ACA was implemented, pharma companies predominantly benefited from new patients coming into the market. We did not see a similar spike in med tech or diagnostics demand from ACA expansion. If we did not see that benefit then, I do not think we will see downside now if Medicaid enrollment changes. For med-tech surgical procedures in the United States, Medicare, not Medicaid, is by far the largest payer for devices. For us, it is over two-thirds of our U.S. cardiovascular business. Another reason this is not a concern is that not all health care products are the same. Demand for high-acuity, life-saving products is very inelastic. In the U.S., we treat people with serious acute medical conditions, and the system does not save lives only of those with insurance. That is why we did not see the same impact with ACA expansion. Many parts of our portfolio are tied to major chronic conditions like diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and cancer, which are less likely to be foregone because of insurance status. Our data is also not showing a decline. I'm not referring just to weekly sales; we look ahead. One benefit of our diversified model is that it provides a holistic view of the entire health care system, not just in the U.S. but globally. Our instruments are located across the country and around the world, and testing volumes in the U.S. have held up very well, including in states with the highest levels of ACA disenrollment. Our U.S. core lab business has accelerated growth in the last two quarters; it was about 7.5% this quarter. If you unpack that, our business selling instruments and reagents for hospital-based testing was up 13% this quarter. So if you look at diagnostics as a forward-looking indicator, we are not seeing a decline. Our U.S. cardiovascular business is performing very well, and we are seeing similar strong, stable demand internationally, in both developed and emerging markets. Demographics also support demand: every day in the United States, about 10,000 people turn 65, and age is a driving factor of health care utilization. So overall, I feel very good about the health care markets, especially the markets where we compete.

transcript.speaker: Robert Marcus
transcript.title: Analyst (JPMorgan)
transcript.content: That is great to hear. Just a quick follow-up, one Abbott specific. It was good to see a small beat on organic sales in the second quarter. The forecast includes an acceleration in the third and fourth quarters. I would love to hear how you are feeling about the confidence level in that acceleration in the second half and if you don't mind just highlighting some of the key growth drivers that get you there. Thanks a lot.

transcript.speaker: Robert Ford
transcript.title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
transcript.content: Sure. I'm feeling very confident, and that confidence is driven by the hard work the team is doing. Q2 results showed we have momentum building; our growth rate stepped up to mid-single digits from low single digits in the previous two quarters. Sales growth accelerated each month during the quarter. For the second half, the lift is driven primarily by four areas: Nutrition, electrophysiology, core lab, and cancer diagnostics. Each of these businesses is entering the second half with momentum and clear drivers of growth. Nutrition is tracking slightly ahead of expectations with strategies around pricing, new product launches, and commercial execution performing well. Electrophysiology has strong launch activity and good feedback on our new products. Our core lab business performed well globally; although China VBP caused a sizable portion of our international decline over several quarters, that impact is moderating to mid-single digits, allowing other businesses to overpower the China impact. Cancer diagnostics also has very good trajectory, especially with new Cologuard users exceeding expectations and care-gap programs ramping volumes. So those four areas represent the significant shift driving second-half acceleration. All other businesses also need to continue to perform, but if I focus on what will move the needle in the second half, it is these four areas, and they are entering Q3 with strong momentum, some slightly ahead of our prior expectations. We feel good about the second-half acceleration.

transcript.speaker: Operator
transcript.title: Operator
transcript.content: Thank you. Our next question comes from Larry Biegelsen from Wells Fargo. Your line is open.

transcript.speaker: Larry Biegelsen
transcript.title: Analyst (Wells Fargo)
transcript.content: Good morning. Thanks for taking the question. Robert, I would love to double-click on Libre. If you could talk about Libre trends in the U.S. and international markets. You reported worldwide growth of 9.5%. What is the outlook for the CGM business for the remainder of this year? What is your latest thinking on U.S. timing for the dual glucose-ketone sensor and type 2 non-insulin coverage? Can these accelerate CGM growth or just maintain the current rate? Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Robert Ford
transcript.title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
transcript.content: Sure, Larry. I understand the point about 9.5% on a $2 billion quarterly business. Let me unpack the market and where we see opportunities. I'm very bullish on this market. We estimate 75 to 80 million people around the world could realistically be on a CGM, and only about 15 million are using it today. There's still significant opportunity for sustainable growth and acceleration. The most immediate driver is reimbursement expansion. We are in active discussions with a dozen or so countries to introduce or expand reimbursement, driven by the robust clinical data showing benefits such as lower A1c, reduced hospitalizations, and more time in range. The challenge is timing; it's difficult to pinpoint the exact month or quarter when reimbursement expansions will occur. Until major reimbursement changes occur, the market can seem to plateau at mid- to high-single-digit growth, which on a $2 billion quarterly base is still a strong business. When reimbursement expands—as we've seen historically—growth accelerates materially. The U.S. type 2 opportunity is particularly large, potentially unlocking around 10 million Medicare beneficiaries and accelerating commercial coverage. That could be a multibillion-dollar opportunity and could happen in the fall, but I cannot forecast the exact timing. International coverage expansions in sizable markets like France, Japan, and Canada are already in place, and there are several other significant markets under discussion. Because of the scale and potential, we are already planning for additional manufacturing capacity. Our fourth sensor facility came online around 2024 and is a 100 million sensor facility; we anticipate capacity pressure in the next couple of years and are evaluating a fifth facility, which would be a significant investment potentially approaching a billion dollars. Regarding the dual glucose-ketone sensor approval timelines, discussions are in very advanced stages but I will not attempt to forecast the exact timing. As soon as we have approvals, we will announce them. We are hearing positive feedback from early European users of Libre Duo. Overall, we feel very good about the market, the company’s position, the investments we're making, and the variety of growth drivers, including reimbursement expansion and product innovation.

transcript.speaker: Larry Biegelsen
transcript.title: Analyst (Wells Fargo)
transcript.content: Thanks for the comprehensive answer. Just to set the record straight, I was not criticizing the 9.5%; I was clarifying. Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Operator
transcript.title: Operator
transcript.content: Thank you. Our next question will come from Vijay Kumar from Evercore ISI. Your line is open.

transcript.speaker: Vijay Kumar
transcript.title: Analyst (Evercore ISI)
transcript.content: Hi, Robert. Good morning and thank you for taking my question. I wanted to dive a little bit on Exact Sciences. The business did, as you noted, slightly north of 13%. I think you are assuming a step-up in the back half, maybe 16% plus. A lot of that is driven by pricing and care gap. How much visibility do you have on care-gap programs stepping up for Exact Sciences in the back half? Also, the PREENOM just presented their redo data where advanced adenoma detection rate was north of 18%, well above the competition. When thinking about the blood side of CRC screening, do you still expect Abbott to be the market leader on the blood side even though your entry into the market will be slightly behind? Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Robert Ford
transcript.title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
transcript.content: Sure. We grew about 13% in the first half. The deal model we put together for the acquisition had mid-teens growth for 2026, and I feel confident we will achieve that. The model called for a stronger second half than first half, and the integration is going very well. The team at Exact Sciences has a deep understanding of the market. Care-gap volumes do ramp in the second half and will help drive the acceleration; care-gap programs help health systems achieve HEDIS credit and star ratings, and that work is often done in the second half as health systems focus on their scores. We have good visibility into those programs through the market-access work and discussions with health systems. Price is also an element, and the transition from Cologuard to Cologuard Plus is a modest tailwind. Other growth drivers include new Cologuard users, which are exceeding expectations, a growing rescreen funnel of repeat users, investments in CancerGuard and MRD programs, international expansion, and the addition of a blood test to the portfolio. Blood tests are more convenient but typically have lower sensitivity for precancerous polyps and early-stage detection than stool-based tests like Cologuard. We believe having both stool and blood tests in our portfolio will be powerful: blood tests can bring previously unscreened patients into the screening funnel, and we can then educate and guide them to the more sensitive stool-based test where appropriate. Overall, the integration is progressing well, and I am impressed with the Exact Sciences team and their market plans.

transcript.speaker: Operator
transcript.title: Operator
transcript.content: Thank you. Our next question will come from Matt Taylor from Jefferies. Your line is open.

transcript.speaker: Matt Taylor
transcript.title: Analyst (Jefferies)
transcript.content: Hi. Good morning. Thanks for taking the question. I thought it would be worth spending a minute on EP given you have this series of launches. You seem to be gaining traction with Bolt already. Could you comment on market dynamics and your aspirations in the market? Maybe talk about how you think the AF market will continue to grow, your commitment to growing above the market in the second half, how that could continue into next year, and the kind of share aspirations you have?

transcript.speaker: Robert Ford
transcript.title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
transcript.content: Sure. I'm not going to give specific share targets today, but we do expect to grow faster than the market and begin to capture share. We saw early signs of that in Q2 with sales increasing every month in the quarter. The transition from limited market release to full market release of Bolt in the U.S. in the third quarter, coupled with continued international rollout of Tactiflex Duo, will be important. Feedback from physicians has been very positive. Bolt's integration with mapping systems and better lesion durability are key advantages. Bolt helps address ASC adoption because of the open footprint of the mapping system and the ability to perform cases without general anesthesia. Tactiflex Duo leverages the well-liked Tactiflex chassis with a seamless transition between PFA and RF. We saw more than 20% EP growth in Europe in Q2. Our strategy is to sell the entire procedure—mapping systems, catheters, diagnostics, introducers, ICE catheters—so we position ourselves as a full-procedure provider. We continue to invest in mapping to maintain superiority as competitors introduce their systems. I expect global EP growth to accelerate in the second half and for the momentum we are building this year to carry into next year. Additional boosts will come from new devices like our next-generation LAA device, and continued rollout of Tactiflex Duo and Bolt in the U.S.

transcript.speaker: Operator
transcript.title: Operator
transcript.content: Thank you. Our next question comes from Travis Steed from BofA Securities. Your line is open.

transcript.speaker: Travis Steed
transcript.title: Analyst (BofA Securities)
transcript.content: Hey, Robert. Thanks for taking the question. As we move into the second half of this year, investors are going to start looking more into next year. How do you think about the Abbott portfolio in 2027 if this is a year that sets up for better growth? You have easier nutrition comps, expanding coverage in Libre, EP accelerating, Amulet 360 launching. How do you think about Abbott's growth in 2027?

transcript.speaker: Robert Ford
transcript.title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
transcript.content: It is a little early to give exact 2027 guidance, but we always target a sustainable top-line growth rate in the mid-single digits to high single digits, with EPS growth in the high single digits to double digits. Historically, I have referenced 7% as a sustainable growth target, and I believe that remains appropriate despite the larger company base. If you look at our segments, a reasonable way to think about the portfolio: Nutrition in a 2% to 4% range, Diagnostics with Exact Sciences and moderating VBP impact in China in the 7% to 8% range, EPD at 7% to 9%, and MedTech at 8% to 10%. Collectively, that implies a mid-to-high single-digit growth rate overall, so 7% is a reasonable target. We are also focused on product and clinical pipelines that will contribute in 2029-2030 and beyond. So while we focus on executing in the second half of 2026, we are also planning for sustainable growth into 2027 and beyond.

transcript.speaker: Operator
transcript.title: Operator
transcript.content: Our next question comes from Josh Jennings from TD Cowen. Your line is open.

transcript.speaker: Josh Jennings
transcript.title: Analyst (TD Cowen)
transcript.content: Hi. Good morning. Thanks for the question. Wanted to ask on the Structural Heart unit. I think your team has said it may take time for the U.S. franchise to regain its foundation. Any help thinking through strategic initiatives on commercial infrastructure, pricing, or innovation with the balloon-expandable TAVR and mitral replacement valve in development? When can Structural Heart start to see improved growth trends? Is that 2027 or sooner? Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Robert Ford
transcript.title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
transcript.content: I expect Structural Heart to be back to mid- to high-single-digit growth by the end of the year. Where we've fallen short is not price or product; it's how we approach and compete in the mitral space in the U.S. Competitive intensity has increased, and we've made personnel and approach changes. We have one of the most comprehensive Structural Heart portfolios, and the team is working to better position that full portfolio. We're seeing solid growth in tricuspid, TAVR in the U.S., and international teams have grown double digits for the first half with TAVR up about 30% internationally. The U.S. organization can learn from international strategies. We have important pipeline assets—Cephia mitral replacement valve heading into trials, promising feedback, and potential for significant opportunity. In the short term, it's about commercial execution improvements, and I have confidence in the team to deliver. I would expect meaningful improvement into late 2026 and continued momentum into 2027.

transcript.speaker: Operator
transcript.title: Operator
transcript.content: Our next question comes from Joanne Wuensch from Citi. Your line is open.

transcript.speaker: Joanne Wuensch
transcript.title: Analyst (Citi)
transcript.content: Good morning, and thank you for taking the question. On nutrition, the guidance commentary of 2% to 4% is a nice acceleration off the last couple of quarters. Can you give a state of the union on launching new products and market positioning? Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Robert Ford
transcript.title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
transcript.content: Absolutely. We remain on track with our plan. There are several proof points giving us confidence in the 2% to 4% range. Sequentially, nutrition grew by $125 million, and the month-to-month trend was improving. On the pediatric side, international pediatric sales are back to back positive growth and are currently the highest in the last two years. U.S. pediatric benefits from recent WIC contract wins, and we are now market leader in WIC and non-WIC segments. In adult nutrition, volume has responded positively to price actions taken late last year: U.S. retail consumption of Ensure is up double digits versus our exit of 2025, the highest year-over-year consumption growth we've seen in a year and a half. International adult nutrition is growing sequentially and approaching prior-year levels. New product innovations are contributing, including Ensure versions with higher protein and lower sugar. Upcoming launches include a collagen protein shake, a new adult product with protein, HMB, and creatine, and a new infant formula using whole milk in the second half. Execution remains key, and if momentum continues, there may be opportunity to revisit guidance, but for now the team is executing to plan.

transcript.speaker: Operator
transcript.title: Operator
transcript.content: We will take one more question. Our last question comes from Robby Thibault from BTIG. Your line is open.

transcript.speaker: Robby Thibault
transcript.title: Analyst (BTIG)
transcript.content: Hi. Good morning. Thanks for taking my question. I wanted to circle back on Amulet and the left atrial appendage closure market. You have an exciting product catalyst ahead with Amulet 360. What is Abbott seeing in the market today? Your competitor has mentioned some challenges; what's the appetite for LAA closure today? Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Robert Ford
transcript.title: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
transcript.content: This is a very attractive market, which is why we continue to invest. It's roughly a $2 billion market today and the competitor has about 90% share. Our focus is market share capture. Data and feedback on Amulet 360 have been excellent. The device provides an improved sealing performance and a more seamless implant experience for physicians. LAA closure is increasingly an EP-driven procedure, and a meaningful portion of growth comes from concomitant procedures. We believe having a strong LAA device in our portfolio, alongside leading PFA catheters and mapping systems, positions Abbott well. That's part of why we moved the LAA portfolio into our EP business. We will essentially relaunch the product with Amulet 360, leverage lessons learned, and I am confident this will be a growth driver in 2027 and beyond. There may also be opportunities to expand concomitant procedures into interventional cardiology, not just EP, which could further develop the market. We're excited to bring the next-generation product to market and to compete for share. To close, we are making good progress addressing short-term and temporary challenges we highlighted in January. We are entering the second half with momentum across several key growth drivers. We remain focused on gross margin expansion through mix and cost mitigation, which has given us confidence to raise full-year EPS guidance. Cash generation and cash flow are ahead of our January forecast, providing flexibility for capital return. I'm excited about the pipeline and the product launches over the next 24 months, which give us confidence that the momentum we're building is sustainable into 2027 and 2028. Thank you for joining us today and for your questions.

transcript.speaker: Operator
transcript.title: Operator
transcript.content: This now concludes Abbott's conference call. A webcast replay of this call will be available after 11:00 AM Central Time today on our website, abbott.com. Thank you for joining us today. This concludes today's conference call. You may now disconnect. Everyone, have a wonderful day.
